text:
maria: thinking about provisioning a small "compact" GPU nodepool in us-west3 for low-latency inference QA and burst traffic. goal: warm prefix caching + cheap burst capacity for night jobs. need input on sizing, instance types, quotas, and autoscaler settings.

jon: what are the target p99 and average qps? also, are these single-GPU pods or multi-GPU?

maria: p99 target ~120ms for small chat requests, qps typical ~50 with spikes to 350 for 10m windows. pods request 1 GPU, 32GB RAM, 100GB ephemeral disk. most use mixed-precision, so A10-ish performance preferred.

sanjay: sounds like 1 GPU per pod is fine. i'd do a mixed pool: 4 x a10g-equivalent preemptible and 2 x a10g-equivalent guaranteed (reserved) to keep a steady baseline. if quota short, fallback to t4-like for cheap burst but watch perf delta.

akshay: FYI quota check - us-west3 GPU quota is tight. I ran `gcloud compute regions describe us-west3 --format=json | jq '.quotas[] | select(.metric=="GPUS")'` earlier, we have 14 GPUs free for A10 family.

ops-bot: quota-check: {"region":"us-west3","gpu_a10_quota_total":"48","gpu_a10_quota_used":"34","gpu_a10_quota_remaining":"14"} (via ops-bot)

maria: thanks. proposal: create node-pool named "infer-compact-burst" with autoscaler min=0 max=8, mixed-instance-policy: prefer a10g preemptible for cost, fallback to t4-like spot if preemptible exhausted, and 2 guaranteed nodes of a10g reserved for baseline. Add taint `infer=reserved:NoSchedule` for baseline nodes.

jon: also add labels `workload=inference, tier=burst` and use node-affinity in the deployment. make sure GPU device plugin + nvidia-driver-daemonset is installed before scaling.

maria: example create command (GKE):
```
gcloud container node-pools create infer-compact-burst \
  --cluster=prod-gke-us-west3 \
  --machine-type=a2-highgpu-1g \
  --num-nodes=0 \
  --enable-autoscaling --min-nodes=0 --max-nodes=8 \
  --node-labels=workload=inference,tier=burst \
  --metadata="disable-legacy-endpoints=true" \
  --node-taints=infer=burst:NoSchedule \
  --preemptible
```
(note: we'll adapt machine-type to provider naming; this is illustrative)

sanjay: don't forget to set `--max-surge=1 --max-unavailable=0` for node pool rolling updates if we put reserved nodes there. also suggest local-ssd for the baseline nodes since prefix cache is disk-heavy.

maria: saw this in QA earlier: pods were stuck with `0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient gpu` for a couple minutes while autoscaler woke up. log: 
```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age    From               Message
  ----     ------             ----   ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   2m12s  default-scheduler  0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient gpu.
```
we need faster scale-up + warm baseline.

akshay: autoscaler warm-up: set node group target size to 2 (baseline) for reserved nodes, and keep the burst pool min=0. use node-provisioning with a short priority to pre-provision on small usage signals (if cloud provider supports). Also ensure IAM quotas for createInstance calls are not hitting per-minute limits.

jon: for faster scale we can: 1) use smaller instance types to spin up more nodes faster, 2) tune cluster-autoscaler flags `--scale-up-delay` and `--expander=priority` and 3) enable node-provisioning for instant nodes. But smaller instances may hurt p99. tradeoff.

maria: cost check: rough hourly cost for a10g-like preemptible ~ $0.30/hr, reserved baseline 2 nodes ~ $1.2/hr each. if max 8 nodes at peak, worst-case ~ $6-8/hr preemptible + 2 reserved ~ $2.4/hr => ~ $10/hr peak. monthly depends on duty cycle. anyone want to correct my numbers?

sanjay: numbers look ok for a quick estimate. we should also account for NAT egress + disk IO. local-ssd increases cost but can reduce cache misses.

maria: security/networking: we need to ensure the node-pool lives in the inference VPC with egress rules to redis cache in us-west3. also annotate nodes with `redwood/egress-nat=true` so egress assignment prefers pool with NAT IP.

akshay: +1 on NAT annotation. also please add KMS key binding for node service account per compliance.

maria: will open infra ticket for provisioning + quota uplift if needed. planning to request 10 additional A10 quota to be safe.

deploy-bot: Created ticket INFRA-1842: "provision infer-compact-burst pool in us-west3 + quota uplift request" — https://tickets.redwood.ai/INFRA-1842

jon: fine to proceed when ticket approved. can we add a simple smoke test to automatically call the endpoint and validate p99 < 200ms post-provision?

maria: yep i'll add a nightly job and a scale-exercise script to warm caches: `./scripts/scale_burst.sh --target=350 --duration=600` that will exercise autoscaler.

sanjay: 👍 also add a rollback plan: if spot eviction rate > 20% or p99 jumps > 2x, route traffic to cpu-fallback endpoint.

maria: sounds good. thanks all, i'll draft the pool config and attach to the ticket.

akshay: approving baseline plan. please include cost forecast in the ticket before prod deploy. :thumbsup:
